ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All shareholders, directors, UBOs, signatories, and counterparties must be screened before incorporation against the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit consolidated lists, United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, EU restrictive measures, and national sanctions maintained under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. PEPs, including foreign and domestic senior officials, court and military officers, political party leaders, senior central bankers, and close associates, require automated alert handling, manager approval, enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth verification, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Negative news and adverse media checks must be documented. Any sanctions, PEP, or criminal-integrity alert without adequate justification requires refusal, termination, and a suspicious transaction report to KoFIU.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Office (IROS) of the Supreme Court of Korea
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be registered in Hangul (Korean script) under the Commercial Act. A foreign-language trade name may be presented as a secondary name after the Hangul name. The core name must be followed by Chusik Hoesa or an equivalent corporate identifier. Hanja may be placed in parentheses only as a transliteration aid. The four-tier naming convention comprises Hangul, Hanja, Romanized phonetic transliteration, and foreign trade name; the transliteration must be unique and must not be confused with any existing registered company, trademark, or protected trade name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the court registration officer rejects the proposed name, the applicant may correct the name and refile online. To contest, submit a written objection within 14 days from receipt of the rejection under the Non-Contentious Cases Litigation Procedure. The objection must include a comparative table of existing registered names, proof of distinctiveness, and a statement that no prohibited token is embedded. If the district court maintains rejection, re-file under a materially different name because the Commercial Act does not create a merit-based appellate right for name refusals; an extraordinary administrative appeal to the Supreme Court registration supervision office may be attempted but is rarely granted.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a Chusik Hoesa engaged in general re-invoicing, a commercial virtual office can satisfy the Commercial Act registered-office requirement if it is a licensed service provider with a physical suite, attended reception during business hours, and contractual right to use the address. A mere P.O. mailbox or non-attended address will be rejected by the National Tax Service and by licensed banks for VAT registration, payroll, corporate account opening, and cross-border payment rails. The company must retain complete books and records at the address, display a nameplate, and maintain employment or agency substance. For a re-invoicing hub, an unstaffed virtual address materially impairs tax residence and bank AML/KYC approval.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: physical presence of personnel, original lease contract, nameplate and signage, books and records kept locally, corporate seal custody procedures, active business email/phone, registered director at office, and client contract binders. Risk for a new re-invoicing entity is moderate-to-high because tax authorities treat re-invoicing as a substance-risk structure. Unannounced physical inspection likelihood is approximately 40 to 60 percent within the first 12 months if the registered address is a serviced office without a dedicated employee; higher if the company files VAT refunds, makes large cross-border invoices, or changes registered address within the first reporting period.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), particularly Articles 288 to 317 on incorporation and registration, Articles 329 and 331 on par value and shares, and Articles 361 to 373 on the board of directors; Foreign Investment Promotion Act, Articles 2 and 4; and the Commercial Registration Rules
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, accessible through the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (iRO) at www.iro.go.kr
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Corporation (Chusik Hoesa) under Article 317(1) of the Commercial Act, with the notarized Articles of Incorporation, capital deposit certificate, and officer consent forms attached
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital exists under the Commercial Act, but each share must have a par value of at least KRW 100 and the total subscription

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS). The statutory electronic registration and filing portal is the Home Tax Service (HTS) at www.hometax.go.kr. Cross-border goods clearance is administered by the Korea Customs Service (KCS) through the UNI-PASS electronic trade portal (unipass.customs.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Korean-resident Chusik Hoesa, the entity must obtain a 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN), which serves as both the corporate tax ID and VAT ID, from the competent NTS district office within 20 days of business commencement. The application is submitted through the Home Tax Service portal or at the local district office and must include the articles of incorporation, statutory shareholding and board documentation, evidence of domestic registered address, and initial business plan. For a foreign non-resident entity that has a Korean VAT registration obligation because it maintains a domestic place of business, makes taxable supplies in Korea, or qualifies under the special VAT regime for foreign suppliers of electronic services, the procedure requires: (1) confirmation of Korean nexus; (2) appointment of an authorized Korean tax representative if no domestic place of business exists; (3) submission of the authentic foreign registration certificate, articles of association, power of attorney, passport or equivalent identity documents of the signatory, and evidence of the domestic or deemed place of business; (4) submission of the business registration application through the Home Tax Service or the district office with jurisdiction over the registered business address; (5) receipt of the 10-digit Business Registration Number and official Business Registration Certificate; and (6) designation of a Korean bank account for VAT refund and foreign exchange settlement. The BRN is the unified national TIN for corporate income tax, VAT, withholding tax, and customs transactions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Republic of Korea does not operate a check-the-box election or a separate entity classification election for a Chusik Hoesa. A Korean stock corporation is mandatorily taxed as an entity-level resident corporation on its worldwide income. No hybrid mismatch entity-classification election is available; Korean anti-hybrid rules are applied by statute, not by taxpayer election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) regulated by the Korean Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general economic turnover threshold triggers VAT registration in South Korea. Registration is mandatory before a taxable person commences any VATable business in Korea. A simplified taxable person regime applies to certain small individual entrepreneurs with annual taxable supplies not exceeding KRW 80,000,000. Foreign suppliers of electronic services are subject to mandatory VAT registration from the first taxable supply, with an administrative criterion of prior-year or projected Korean remote-service turnover exceeding KRW 300,000,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Korea does not operate real-time pre-clearance fiscal stamping in the manner of fully digital revenue-capture jurisdictions. Instead, every registered taxable person must issue a valid tax invoice for each taxable supply of goods or services, and corporate taxable persons plus certain small businesses above the statutory e-issuance threshold must transmit an electronic tax invoice (e-tax invoice) to the NTS through the Home Tax Service portal or an NTS-approved EDI/API integrator by no later than the end of the day following issuance. The e-tax invoice must contain the 10-digit BRN of the supplier and customer, supply date, description, quantity, supply value, VAT amount, and applicable zero-rating code. NTS automatically cross-matches purchase and sales e-tax invoices, import and export customs data, cash receipt data, and banking payment information to detect fictitious invoicing, omitted revenues, and false zero-rating claims. There is no government-issued anti-fraud digital stamp or QR fiscal pre-approval requirement for ordinary B2B invoices, but severe statutory penalties apply for failure to transmit e-tax invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for exported goods that physically depart from Korea under an export declaration accepted by the Korea Customs Service. Zero-rating is also available for certain foreign-currency-earning services performed outside Korea or consumed by a non-resident, including international transportation, overseas construction and installation services, and export trade intermediary or re-invoicing services supplied to non-resident customers, provided the service is not consumed in Korea and the consideration is received in convertible foreign currency. For a commercial re-invoicing hub, the 0% VAT claim requires evidence that the Korean intermediary services are rendered to a non-resident principal, that the underlying trade movement is outside Korea or is a certified Korean export, and that the foreign-exchange invoice flow is in hard currency. If title and possession of goods pass entirely outside Korea without any Korean customs export declaration, the supply is generally outside the Korean VAT territorial scope rather than zero-rated, and the file must document that no Korean VAT is imposed. Qualifying offshore digital services supplied by a Korean business to a non-resident customer are zero-rated when the B2B service is supplied to a person without a Korean place of business and the effective use and benefit occur outside Korea.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) accepted by the Korea Customs Service
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill or equivalent multimodal transport document
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or equivalent Korean bank foreign-exchange receipt certificate
Commercial invoice, packing list, purchase order and re-invoicing contract evidencing the foreign-currency trade
Zero-rated electronic tax invoice transmitted to NTS with the statutory zero-rate code and cross-reference to the export declaration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS audit review of export zero-rating combines the zero-rated e-tax invoice, customs export declaration, bill of lading, FIRC, bank settlement ledger, foreign-exchange transaction reports, and the underlying trade contract. If the zero-rated supply is not substantiated, or export proceeds are not repatriated and liquidated in accordance with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the applicable settlement deadlines, NTS may retrospectively claw back the 0% rate and assess output VAT at 10% on the full supply value, plus statutory interest for late payment under the National Tax Collection Act. Additional penalty tax is imposed under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act for underreporting, nontaxable misdeclaration, and fraudulent zero-rating claims, with penalty rates escalating from 20% of the unpaid tax for erroneous omission to 40% for fraudulent evasion; criminal proceedings may also be initiated under the Korean Tax Crimes Punishment Act. The national tax assessment limitation period is generally five years, extended to ten years for fraudulent or other willful concealment, meaning previously refunded VAT remains subject to audit and clawback within the applicable statutory window.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK), acting in conjunction with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and the Financial Services Commission (FSC) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, with the Bank of Korea operating the cross-border settlement supervision and Foreign Exchange Information System.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a broadly liberalized current account with free convertibility for genuine trade, services, and unilateral transfers, but the Korean won is not a fully free-floating offshore-deliverable currency. Bona fide trade payments can be converted by licensed domestic banks upon presentation of invoices, contracts, and customs declaration evidence. Capital account transactions such as foreign direct investment contributions, intercompany loan advances, and equity issuance of a Chusik Hoesa require declaration or prior approval through the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act framework and FIPA reporting to MOEF. Profit remittances, including dividends, are permissible after corporate tax settlement is evidenced, but the remitting bank will demand a certificate of tax payment, audited financial statements, a board resolution declaring the dividend, and a completed foreign exchange payment report. There is no forced surrender of export proceeds to the central bank; exporters may retain foreign currency in authorized foreign currency deposit accounts. However, the KRW's offshore market is limited, and onshore hedging through forwards or swaps is subject to the real-demand principle and underlying trade exposure. For a re-invoicing hub, capital verification of inbound equity and the clean documentation of each payables/receivables leg are the most material convertibility hurdles.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Article 5 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Export Settlement Regulations, export proceeds must be collected within 180 days from the date of export declaration or the date of shipment, whichever is applicable, unless an extension is granted by the head of the handling bank or MOEF for exceptional mercantile circumstances. There is no mandatory conversion ratio: the exporter may hold foreign currency receipts indefinitely in a designated Foreign Currency Deposit Account at a licensed domestic bank, without converting them into Korean won. If the export claim remains unsettled past the statutory deadline, the bank must require a written explanation, may record the overdue claim, and may convert the outstanding receivable into KRW through the borrower's domestic account after reporting to the relevant authority. All export proceeds must be reported through the Foreign Exchange Information System or Korea Customs Service settlement records, and each designated bank must maintain the supporting trade documents for AML/CFT and balance-of-payments reporting.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account for Foreign Direct Investment (KRW/USD)
Basic Operational Currency Account with Treasury FX Desk
Export Settlement Foreign Currency Account and Trade Services
Operational KRW Account with Trade Finance and Documentary Collection

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to nil. South Korean law does not treat offshore fintech EMI platforms as licensed banks for KRW clearing, foreign exchange settlement, or corporate account opening. The Financial Services Commission and the Bank of Korea require deposit-taking and foreign exchange activities to be performed through domestically licensed banking institutions or registered payment service providers with a clear partnership with a domestic bank. An offshore EMI cannot issue a KRW IBAN, cannot execute a SWIFT MT103 with a Korean purpose code, and cannot give the Chusik Hoesa a defendable FX reporting trail. At best, an EMI could be used as an ancillary cross-border collection tool if the funds are immediately swept into the entity's domestic Tier-1 bank account, but the core treasury infrastructure must remain with a Korean licensed commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Chusik Hoesa with non-resident statutory directors, Tier-1 Korean banks require at least one physical in-branch appearance by the representative director or an expressly authorized director to conduct a video-recorded onboarding interview, sign the account mandate, verify the corporate seal and passport, and establish the ultimate beneficial owner structure. Remote onboarding with an apostilled or consular-legalized power of attorney is sometimes permitted for the initial signature package, but the bank will generally require the director to appear within a fixed window for the final risk interview. A proxy-only opening without any physical presence is rarely accepted for a foreign-owned trade intermediary due to the enhanced AML risk. In practice, a domestically resident corporate officer or a professional director is strongly recommended to satisfy the bank's face-to-face KYC requirement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors combined with a multi-layered beneficial ownership chain that obscures who controls the re-invoicing entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copies of the home-country company registry, apostilled notarised passports for all directors and shareholders, an updated register of members, a formal beneficial ownership declaration identifying every individual above 10% through each intermediate entity, a group organizational chart, signed economic substance documentation, and the account's intended transaction profile with projected volumes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: A payment-flow/goods-flow mismatch typical of re-invoicing hubs, where first-party logistics are absent and settlement does not correspond to a single clear import/export voyage.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master supply agreements, purchase orders, commercial invoices, packing lists, third-party transport documents (bills of lading, air waybills, CMR notes), customs declarations at both origin and destination, warehouse receipts or inspection certificates, and a visually documented trade flow map explaining the physical goods movement against the re-invoicing payment arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid transaction velocity with very thin gross margins, which resembles smurfing, pass-through settlement, or trade-based money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements for at least two prior fiscal years or the entity's projected financials if newly incorporated, profit-margin analysis consistent with the re-invoicing model, transfer pricing documentation including a Korean local file and master file, bank statements from the original jurisdiction, a granular business plan with settlement cycle charts, and an independent accountant's letter describing the commercial purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and high-risk jurisdiction exposure in the counterparty set, especially where downstream buyers or upstream suppliers are domiciled in monitored or embargoed regions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete counterparty KYC files, transaction-specific sanctions screening results with hit-resolution narratives, compliance certificates from each major counterparty confirming no sanctioned goods, proof of goods' country of origin, valid trade control licenses, and contractual clauses that prohibit resale of goods to sanctioned parties or through prohibited payment corridors.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity for the Chusik Hoesa must be routed as a SWIFT MT103 from the foreign investor's bank to the designated Korean bank account opened under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The remittance must be labelled with the Korean foreign exchange purpose code for equity capital acquisition or foreign direct investment, and a FIPA foreign investment report must be lodged with the designated bank before or immediately after the transfer. The bank will hold the remittance in a capital escrow or designated foreign currency account and issue a capital verification certificate after the amount is credited and the share issuance resolution is filed. Conversion into KRW for operational liquidity is permitted only via the licensed bank's FX desk and must be matched to the actual cash flow needs of the entity. All inbound remittances must include a proper SWIFT Sender Reference and a structured narrative referencing the entity ID and the FIPA report number.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound supplier and trade settlement payments will be executed through SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for open-account and re-invoiced payables, commercial letters of credit (sight or usance) transmitted via SWIFT MT700 for documentary trade, and documentary collections on D/P or D/A basis using the bank's receiving and paying instruments. MT202 cover payments will be used for interbank reimbursement where required. Every outgoing payment must be supported by a valid underlying contract, commercial invoice, transport or receipt confirmation, and a Korean foreign exchange payment report prepared by the bank. For KRW-denominated settlements to non-resident counterparties, the bank will require confirmation of the trade purpose and may require a tax withholding certificate if royalties, interest, or service fees are involved. The bank's trade finance division will execute the LC issuance and collection against the approved treasury mandate and the company's AML/KYC standing.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore FX forward contracts (deliverable and non-deliverable) with a licensed Korean bank, limited to the amount and tenor of the underlying export/import receivables and payables as verified by trade documents.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing USD/KRW for non-resident hedge counterparties where onshore access is not available, but only when the exposure is proven by trade contracts and the NDF is booked with a recognized international bank treasury desk.

Cross-currency swaps for medium-term foreign currency payables and receivables, permitted only when the Chusik Hoesa has a documented physical trade flow, a valid underlying exposure, and a bilateral ISDA/CSA or Korean FX master agreement with a licensed financial institution.

Plain-vanilla FX options for hedging budget-rate protection on large re-invoicing tickets, subject to the bank's real-demand compliance framework and a non-speculative treasury policy approved by the board in the account mandate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and Local Income Tax Surcharge (juridical person tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 of the year immediately following each fiscal year; an extension of up to four months is available upon application and approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-file penalty of 20% of the assessed tax due, underreporting penalty of 10%, non-payment penalty of 0.022% per day on the unpaid amount; prolonged delinquency can lead to tax seizure, business registration cancellation, and compulsory dissolution by court order

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Final VAT Return (preliminary half-year return and annual final settlement)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Preliminary half-year VAT return due July 25; final VAT return for the calendar year due January 25 of the following year (for a December 31 fiscal year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty equal to 10% of unpaid VAT plus additional daily interest at 0.022% per day; for non-filing, a 20% penalty based on tax-included supply value can be imposed

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Financial Statements Approval at Annual General Meeting (AGM)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: The shareholders' meeting (or board of directors if permitted for private companies); minutes kept at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of the fiscal year (e.g., by March 31 for December year-end); public companies must file the approved statement with the Financial Supervisory Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: For private companies, failure to hold the AGM does not create an administrative strike-off but triggers civil liability of directors; for public companies, delisting and fines up to KRW 100 million for non-disclosure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Auditor Appointment and Audit Report Submission (when threshold applies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the External Audit Information Delivery System administered with the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Appoint external auditor within four months after fiscal year-end; submit audit report within six months after fiscal year-end (i.e., by June 30 for December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies is subject to criminal penalties up to 5 years imprisonment or KRW 50 million fine, business restriction, and administrative fines; listed entities may be subject to audit designation by the FSS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Shareholder Registry and Stock Transfer Ledger Updates
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: None - maintained at the company's registered office; if foreign investment is involved, report to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy via KOTRA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Registered immediately upon any transfer; for foreign investments, file a change report within 30 days of the transaction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain the registry may subject the company to a court administrative fine of up to KRW 5 million; failure to file a foreign investment change report may expose the company to fines under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Article 2 of the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, a corporation is required to undergo an independent CPA audit if it triggers any of the following: (1) total assets at fiscal year-end exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9 million); (2) it is a listed company or has adopted K-IFRS; (3) it is designated by the Financial Services Commission because of public interest; (4) it has issued equity-linked securities to 500 or more shareholders; (5) it is a holding company or a quasi-capital finance company. The KRW 12 billion asset threshold is the principal quantitative trigger; revenue and headcount are not standalone triggers but are relevant under the public interest company designation criteria. In addition, banks, financial institutions, and insurance companies are always subject to a statutory audit regardless of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) are mandatory for listed companies and for companies designated under the Act on External Audit; all other corporations may apply Korean Accounting Standards (K-GAAP), with simplified standards available for small and medium-sized companies (SME Korean GAAP).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Republic of Korea does not operate a recurring annual UBO confirmation filing. A Chusik Hoesa must maintain an accurate member registry and update it promptly upon each share transfer; transfers are evidenced by share certificates and endorsement, and the board is obligated to record transfers without delay. For foreign investors licensed under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, any change in original ownership or shareholding must be reported to the relevant ministry through KOTRA within 30 days. There is no national statutory obligation to file an annual beneficial ownership statement, but for FATCA/CRS purposes, financial institutions obtain UBO information through customer due diligence in relation to bank accounts. The corporate register must be available for court inspection and tax inspection for at least 10 years.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Register of Charges/Mortgages, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: For companies below the KRW 12 billion asset threshold and not designated, no statutory audit is required; voluntary CPA appraisals and bookkeeping typically range from $3,000 - $8,000. For mandatory audits, certified audit fees range from $10,000 - $60,000 depending on asset size, transactions, and complexity.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Progressive national corporate income tax: 9% on taxable income up to KRW 200,000,000; 19% on the next band up to KRW 20,000,000,000; 21% on the next band up to KRW 300,000,000,000; and 24% on income exceeding KRW 300,000,000,000. A local income tax surcharge of 10% of the national CIT liability applies, yielding an effective headline range of 9.9% to 26.4%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Available statutory incentives include: (i) Free Economic Zone foreign investment incentives under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act granting 50% CIT exemption for 5 years and 50% reduction for 2 years; (ii) R&D tax credits under the Special Tax Treatment Control Act up to 20% to 30% of qualifying expenditures; (iii) NOL carryforward of 10 years for most corporations; (iv) SME preferential rates in limited manufacturing cases; and (v) no general patent-box regime. A re-invoicing hub typically cannot use production or patent incentives and must rely only on R&D or foreign investment credits if the corporate formalities are satisfied.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Official Korean Corporate Income Tax Return: Form No. 1, Corporate Tax Base and Tax Calculation Statement, together with supplemental schedules (Form Nos. 2 through 58); mandatory e-filing via the National Tax Service HomeTax portal (www.hometax.go.kr).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (for each fiscal year) plus semi-annual interim prepayments when prior-year CIT liability exceeded KRW 10,000,000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed within 3 months after the close of the fiscal year (e.g., March 31 for calendar-year entities); interim prepayment returns are due within 2 months after the first half of the fiscal year. If the filing date falls on a weekend or public holiday, the due date moves to the next business day.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification: legal name, Korean registration number, fiscal year-end, business address, representative director name, industry code, paid-in capital, and shareholder list identifying the ultimate foreign parent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact Korean registration number and corporate name. Provide the foreign parent's country of residence, shareholding percentage, and a copy of the foreign investment report if the foreign owner holds more than 10% under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. All declarations must be in English or Korean; the form should match the tax identification numbers reported under automatic exchange frameworks.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue/gross sales (total gross receipts from business activities). For a re-invoicing hub, this line includes the full invoice value to Korean customers if the Chusik Hoesa takes title to goods; if the entity acts solely as a commissionaire, report the commission income only.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Classify income according to whether the Korean entity purchases and resells as principal or merely invoices on behalf of a foreign principal. A pure pass-through of funds without economic ownership is a red flag. If the hub holds title and bears inventory risk, report the gross revenue and corresponding COGS in Box 3; if the hub acts as an intermediary, entering only the commission keeps the tax base aligned with economic profits and avoids artificial revenue inflation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales, operating expenses, depreciation, amortization, interest expense, royalties, and other deductible costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany purchases must be computed at arm's length for tax purposes. Disallow any royalty or service fee paid to the foreign parent unless a valid, enforceable agreement exists and the fee is economically supported by functions performed and risk assumed. Thin capitalization under the Corporate Income Tax Act (3:1 debt-to-equity for Japanese residents, 6:1 for other foreign shareholders) restricts interest deductions. Cross-border cost allocations must be substantiated with transfer pricing documentation and cannot be shifted toward the Korean entity to artificially reduce taxable profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Book income before tax adjustments; then the computation adds disallowed expenses, deducts tax-exempt income, applies prior-year NOL carryforward, and adjusts for items under the arm's length principle.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the Korean arm's length standard by marking up the re-invoicing service margin using the Transactional Net Margin Method (TNMM) with appropriate benchmarks. Deduct the net operating loss carryforward generated within the last 10 years including losses from the same re-invoicing activity only if the business has economic substance. A re-invoicing hub that reports a loss for several consecutive years while foreign parent profits are high will trigger a NTS economic substance audit and possible denial of NOL carryforward as a sham.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable after applying tax credits, foreign tax credit, prepayments, and interim payments; final amount due or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim foreign tax credits for qualifying foreign-source income taxes paid by the Korean entity, but only if the Korean entity has a foreign PE and the income is real. For non-resident shareholders, the final tax payable must additionally reconcile any withholding tax on dividends or interest paid outward. The entity must attach the certificate of withholding tax paid, Form 22 (Non-Resident Withholding Statement), and the foreign remittance records. Under no circumstance may the dividends paid to foreign shareholders be claimed as a deductible expense.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Supplementary schedule of transactions with foreign related parties, including intercompany sales, purchases, service fees, interest, and royalties; also a declaration of foreign financial accounts with balances exceeding KRW 500,000,000.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must detail each related-party transaction by counterparty, country, amount, and transfer pricing method. For each foreign related party, provide the applicable DTA, the source of the income, and the methodology used (CUP, resale price, cost plus, TNMM, or profit split). The schedule acts as a self-assessment; omission of this schedule is a separate statutory violation that can trigger a 30% additional tax under transfer pricing rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: an additional tax of 0.03% per day of the unpaid tax, capped at 20% of the total unpaid CIT. Understatement: 10% additional tax for negligent underreporting and 40% for intentional or grossly negligent underreporting under the Basic Act for National Taxes. Willful tax evasion with fabricated invoices triggers criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act: imprisonment up to 3 years (or up to 5 years if the evaded tax exceeds KRW 300,000,000), plus a fine up to three times the evaded tax. Failure to withhold on non-resident dividend, interest, or royalty payments: 10% additional tax on the unwithheld amount plus 3.5% per annum interest. Failure to submit transfer pricing documentation: an additional tax equal to 30% of the tax on the adjusted income per Article 8(3) of the Framework Act on International Tax Coordination.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% gross dividend withholding tax (20% national tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge) imposed on dividends paid by a Korean Chusik Hoesa to a non-resident corporate shareholder, unless a reduced rate is available under an applicable bilateral Double Tax Agreement (DTA).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief: (1) obtain an original Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the recipient's foreign tax authority covering the year of payment; (2) submit Form No. 24 (Application for Non-Resident Tax Exemption/Reduction) to the National Tax Service before the payment date, or within three years after the payment to claim a refund; (3) provide a beneficial ownership certificate and a representation that the recipient is not a nominee, agent, or conduit; (4) attach the dividend payment resolution, share register, and bank transfer evidence; (5) for interest and royalties, provide the loan/licence agreement and proof that the underlying services or intangible rights were actually rendered to, and used by, the Korean entity. The NTS will apply the Principal Purpose Test under the MLI and reject treaty relief where the main purpose of the structure is to obtain treaty access without real economic substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory withholding tax is 22% (20% national tax plus 2% local surtax) on gross interest and royalties paid to non-residents. Treaty rates commonly reduce this to 10%–15% for interest (e.g., a 10% rate under the Korea-US and Korea-China treaties) and 5%–15% for royalties (e.g., 10% for United States and 10% for China). For full treaty relief, the foreign payee must present a valid TRC, a Form 24 application, and a beneficial ownership declaration before the Korean withholding agent remits the payment; failure to do so results in the full 22% withholding obligation remaining in force, with penalties for non-withholding.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_local_threshold_local_c: KRW 10,000,000,000 in aggregate cross-border related-party transactions (sales, purchases, services, interest, royalties) during the fiscal year mandates preparation and, upon NTS request, filing of Local File and Master File documentation. Even below this threshold, the NTS has the power to demand any taxpayer to submit transfer pricing documentation within 60 days under Article 8(1) of the Framework Act on International Tax Coordination.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea applies the substance-over-form doctrine under case law and Article 4 of the Framework Act on International Tax Coordination. For a re-invoicing hub, economic substance requires actual employees, physical premises, managerial decision-making, risk-bearing capacity, and the ability to execute independent contractual functions. The Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) concept is embedded in the Korean CFC and international tax rules; if the Chusik Hoesa conducts no business activity other than re-invoicing, the NTS may disregard its separate legal personality and attribute the re-invoicing profit to the foreign principal, resulting in re-characterization of service income as Korean-source and immediate withholding tax liability. The absence of economic substance also exposes the entity to penalties for sham tax avoidance and abuse of DTA benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion through Sham Re-Invoicing / Shell Entity Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean Chusik Hoesa acts as a pure re-invoicing pass-through: it issues invoices to Korean customers for goods or digital content supplied by a foreign related party, without holding inventory, bearing foreign exchange risk, retaining any employees engaged in genuine trading functions, or having a physical office other than a registered agent address. The entity retains a 0.5% commission while the foreign principal captures the real entrepreneurial profit. The NTS examines the transaction under the substance-over-form doctrine and determines that the Korean entity is a transparent conduit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 52 of the Corporate Income Tax Act, the NTS can reallocate income to the foreign principal and deny all artificial deductions; Article 4 of the Framework Act on International Tax Coordination allows disregard of a conduit entity lacking substantive business purpose. The Basic Act for National Taxes Article 47-3 imposes an additional tax of 40% for willful understatement, and the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 3(1) authorizes criminal prosecution with imprisonment up to 3 years (up to 5 years if the evaded tax exceeds KRW 300,000,000) and a fine up to three times the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced under the Basic Act for National Taxes Article 39: a director who intentionally participated in the sham scheme is jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax and additional tax when the company's assets are insufficient. The NTS may impose a travel ban (international blacklisting) against the director through the Framework Act on International Tax Coordination Article 10, and the public prosecutor may institute criminal charges resulting in imprisonment, personal asset seizure, and civil restitution to the Korean Revenue from the director's personal estate.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure and Substance Disregard
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean entity has cross-border intercompany transactions exceeding KRW 10,000,000,000 but prepares no Local File, no Master File, and no economic benchmarking study. Upon the NTS's written request, it refuses to produce transfer pricing documentation within the statutory 60-day deadline. The NTS subsequently applies a downward adjustment under the resale price method, recognizing a 12% profit margin on the re-invoicing turnover and asserting that the foreign parent's profit is Korean-source based on the Korean entity's actual management activities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Pursuant to Article 8(3) of the Framework Act on International Tax Coordination, failure to submit transfer pricing documentation triggers an additional tax equal to 30% of the tax on the adjusted income. If the NTS determines that the missing documentation was intended to conceal an evasion scheme, the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act applies with fines up to KRW 50,000,000 for the corporate entity and additional imprisonment penalties for responsible officers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The CEO and CFO are jointly and severally liable for the additional tax under the joint responsibility provisions of the Basic Act for National Taxes Article 39 when the failure constitutes gross negligence. The NTS can obtain a provisional seizure of the directors' personal bank accounts and real property, issue a departure ban (travel blacklist) preventing the executives from leaving South Korea, and, if the omission is proven willful, the directors face personal criminal prosecution and civil damages from the foreign parent for breaching fiduciary duties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unreported Foreign Account / Unlawful Profit Repatriation and Withholding Tax Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The foreign parent instructs the Korean Chusik Hoesa to distribute profits under the label of a 'share capital reduction' or 'intercompany loan repayment' without any actual economic debt, thereby avoiding Korean withholding tax on dividends. The Korean entity processes a payment of EUR 5,000,000 to the foreign parent through a Hong Kong bank account without withholding the 22% statutory rate, does not submit Form 22 (Non-Resident Withholding Statement), and fails to report the existence of the Hong Kong account as a foreign financial account with the NTS. The NTS detects the transactions through exchange-of-information mechanisms and the Bank for International Settlements data.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A failure to withhold triggers an additional tax of 10% of the unwithheld amount under the Basic Act for National Taxes, plus 3.5% per annum penalty interest. Under-reporting a foreign financial account with a balance exceeding KRW 500,000,000 incurs a fine of up to 20% of the unreported balance (capped at KRW 10,000,000,000) under the Framework Act on International Tax Coordination. The disguised dividend is reclassified as a dividend for withholding tax purposes, leading to the full 22% statutory rate, and the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 3 authorizes imprisonment up to 3 years and fines up to three times the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The Korean representative director who signed the sham loan agreement and authorized the transfer is personally liable for the unwithheld tax and penalty under the joint responsibility doctrine. A criminal indictment can result in imprisonment, a court-ordered travel ban (passport invalidation), and confiscation of the director's personal assets, including residential property, to satisfy the evasion amount. The foreign parent may also bring a civil claim against the director in Korea or in an international arbitration forum for violating corporate governance duties and harming the subsidiary.
